processing: An unoxidised green tea. Its particular method is little documented; as with other Chinese yunwu greens, the leaf is fixed, shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this tea; spring picking is usual for high-mountain yunwu greens.
appearance_dry: Little is documented; yunwu greens are typically fine, tightly shaped and green.
appearance_liquor: Typically pale yellow-green and clear, as with other yunwu greens.
appearance_wet: Typically tender green, as with other high-mountain spring greens.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record exists for this name; yunwu greens of this kind are typically smooth, gentle and lightly sweet.

brewing.notes: General handling for a Chinese spring green tea.

vintage_note: Usual for its class: sold as the current year's harvest, mainly spring, and best drunk within about a year. Early pickings generally cost more. No published standard for this name is widely known.
description:
Dengcun Yunwu is a green tea named after Dengcun township in Yiling district of Yichang, Hubei, in the hills beside the Xiling Gorge of the Yangtze. Yunwu means 'cloud and mist', a name shared by many Chinese mountain greens, so the township is the part that matters.

Dengcun is a serious tea place with large areas of mountain garden, and has been promoted as a 'hometown of famous Chinese tea'. Little is written about how this particular tea is made, so assume the normal green tea steps of fixing, shaping and drying.

No reliable tasting description exists for this name. Mountain greens of this kind are typically smooth and gently sweet, and they brew best in water just off the boil, in short steeps.

If you find it, ask which season and which part of the township it comes from. Yunwu on its own is a loose word, and it says nothing about grade.
history: Little is documented about this tea. Its name appears in lists of Hubei's named green teas, alongside the likes of Enshi Yulu and Xiazhou Bifeng, but no founding date or creator is recorded. The better-documented story is that of Dengcun township as a modern tea-growing area.
